messages:
Maya: Heads-up — found a weird failure mode when onboarding the quantized judge (gpt-j-4q) on the eval runner. Lots of near-ties but the CI tiebreak path seems to flip unpredictably. :thinking:
Sam: Can you paste a short example of the outputs? is it low confidence scores across the board or just disagreement patterns?
Maya: Small example: two candidates, judge scores: candidate A = 0.501, candidate B = 0.499. But when we run the same seed with the quantized judge we sometimes get 0.47/0.53 flip. Looks like entropy jumps.
Arun: That smells like calibration + quant noise in last-layer logits. Our current rubric uses strict max-score selection, then fallback to heuristic ordering. We should prefer a tiebreak that accounts for score uncertainty.
Priya: Agreed. Proposal: introduce an "entropy-aware tiebreak" — compute softmax over judge logits, if max_score - 2nd_score < delta_threshold OR entropy > H_thresh then use alternative metric (e.g., rerankerConsensus or anchor agreement).
Maya: Nice. What should delta_threshold and H_thresh be?
Sam: For starters delta_threshold = 0.02, H_thresh = 1.5 nats (we can tune). Also add a requirement that if quantized judge flips >1% of anchors vs fp16 judge on the anchor set, the model is quarantined from automatic rollouts.
Arun: I'll sketch a rubric snippet we can drop into eval harness.
Arun: ```json
{"rubric_version":"v2.1-quant-tiebreak","primary":"max_score","tiebreak_order":["entropy_aware","anchor_consensus","human_vote"],"entropy_threshold":"1.5","delta_threshold":"0.02","quarantine_rule":{"anchor_flip_rate":0.01,"action":"block+notify"}}
```
Priya: Love the explicit quarantine action. Can we wire CI to fail PRs that change the rubric or add a quantized judge without a manual signoff?
Tim: Yes — CI idea: on any PR that modifies judges or rubric JSON, run a lightweight anchor check job: compare new judge vs baseline on canonical anchor set (N=200), compute flip rate and win-rate delta, and fail if flip_rate > 1% OR win_rate_delta < -0.5%.
Maya: That should catch regressions. Also, add a dashboard alert in Redwood Console: per-judge anchor_flip_rate rolling 24h > 0.5% -> pager to eng-ml on call.
Sam: Quick thought: instead of hard thresholds for rollout blocking maybe use a scoring function that weights flip_rate + entropy_change + bias_checks. But for CI keep it simple and conservative.
Priya: Bias checks — we need to ensure the tiebreak doesn't preferentially pick candidates that increase protected-group disparity. Suggest adding a small set of fairness anchors and require no >2% differential change on fairness metric.
Arun: Good call. I'll add a fairness_anchor_check to the rubric.
Arun: ```json
{"fairness_anchor_check":{"groups":["gender","race","region"],"max_delta":0.02}}
```
Maya: eval-bot ran the recent experiment on staging with the entropy-aware tiebreak enabled. Summary below.
eval-bot: Experiment run 1718000300: anchors=1000, quant_judge_flip_rate=0.012, win_rate_delta=-0.6%, avg_entropy_increase=0.35, fairness_group_max_delta=0.007. Action: QUARANTINE triggered (flip_rate 1.2% > 1%).
Maya: Ok that aligns with the suspicions. We should fix calibration before promoting this judge.
Sam: Short-term mitigation: in the harness, when a quantized judge is quarantined, route to fallback judgement chain: (fp16_ensemble -> heuristic) and annotate result with provenance header.
Priya: I'll update the CI job and add a lightweight integration test that asserts fallback routing is exercised when quarantine flag present.
Tim: I can add the Console alert and a per-judge panel for entropy + flip_rate over time. We should track per-sequence-length stats too (maybe quant noise grows with longer context).
Maya: Thanks all. Action items: Arun: update rubric JSON with entropy tiebreak + fairness check. Priya: CI gating + fallback test. Tim: dashboard + alerts. Sam: draft tuning plan for delta/H thresholds. I'll open a follow-up thread with a small anchor set for tuning. :thumbsup:
